relationship: Each percentage change applies to the current amount, so a repeated multiplier models compound change and its reciprocal reverses it.

learnerLoop.action: Apply percentage changes, derive a multiplier and extend or reverse the calculation.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Successive amounts and the projected sequence update.
learnerLoop.evidence: The value chain, multiplier comparison and working checks show repeated change from a changing base.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Select the multiplier operation needed for the next period or reverse calculation.

invariants: Each new percentage is applied to the previous amount.
A reverse percentage change uses the reciprocal multiplier, not the opposite percentage.
safeAdaptations: Vary positive and negative percentage rates and time horizons.
Adjust working requirements while retaining multiplier-based evidence.
nonGoals: Adding the same absolute percentage amount at every step.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

projection.description: Manual sequence compared with the repeated multiplier; optional horizon extension.
projection.visibility: Forward mode, enabled by the bridge/projection state.

base-rate-periods.description: Starting or final amount, percentage rate and number of periods.
base-rate-periods.domain: Positive amounts (currency £ where the question uses money), signed percentages, integer years.
base-rate-periods.source: Generated givens vary with forward or reverse problem.
base-rate-periods.output: The bars, gates and goal expose the supplied values.

period-changes.description: Each period has its own change amount, applied to that period’s current base.
period-changes.domain: Amount units follow the problem; currency comparisons use the lab’s money tolerance.
period-changes.source: Learner drags the next bar at None or enters indexed change amounts at Some/All.
period-changes.output: A completed gate unlocks the next period and its base.

multiplier-bridge.description: Whole percentage and a unitless forward multiplier are two representations linked by division by 100.
multiplier-bridge.source: Supplied or entered according to Working level.
multiplier-bridge.output: The bridge must match the rate before projection or inverse steps count as complete.

inverse-result.description: An inverse operation and factor recover ONE original amount; operation buttons are alternatives, not two answer slots.
inverse-result.domain: Multiply/divide choice and positive decimal factor.
inverse-result.source: Learner chooses the inverse gate; resulting amount is calculated.
inverse-result.output: The reverse result is compared with the original target.

modes.none: Apply each forward percentage change by dragging the existing next bar. Whole percentage and multiplier are supplied.
modes.some: Enter each forward change and the one-period multiplier; whole percentage is shown.
modes.all: Also derive the whole percentage after the change.
modes.reverse: All levels choose an inverse operation/factor; support supplies or requires the forward percentage/multiplier bridge. The projection horizon is an optional extension.

dependencies: Forward gates are sequential; each percentage is applied to the latest amount, not repeatedly to the opening value.
The percentage-to-multiplier bridge gates dependent multiplier input.
Reverse completion requires the bridge, correct inverse factor/operation and restored original value.
implementation.completion: challengeComplete() requires all forward gates and Working-dependent bridge results, or reverseComplete() for reverse mode.
